guide.title: User guide
guide.intro: Pick a topic from the menu. Every topic ends with three tips for beginners and one tip for advanced users.

groups.title: Getting started
body: L Studio has five screens: Sound, Pad, Drum, Loop, and Mic. The tabs under the scopes switch between them. The top bar stays on every screen: the PRO or LIVE chip, MIDI, WAV, and Settings.

sections.title: Recording MIDI and WAV
body: A tap on MIDI starts a MIDI recording. Another tap stops and asks the phone where to save the file.
A tap on WAV starts recording what you hear. Another tap stops and asks the phone where to save the file.

While MIDI or WAV records, a gold clock in minutes and seconds (MM:SS) shows between the title and the MIDI key. The minutes keep counting past 60. If both record, it counts from the one that started first.

sections.title: LIVE mode
body: PRO is the normal mode, with everything open. LIVE is a mode that locks some buttons, so you can focus on playing. It is good for recording and for performing, because a stray tap cannot clear a take, load a file, or rename a channel.

What LIVE locks: Clear on Looper and Mic channels. Load on the drum rows and on Looper channels. Mic channels have no Load key. In the drum sound list, LOAD, RENAME, and DELETE. Import on the Loop and Mic screens, and Import in Drum styles. Typing a number on a knob, while a drag still works. The names of Looper and Mic channels, the Looper page name, and the long-press that opens Page name.

What LIVE leaves open: Rec, Play, Stop, M, S, Redo, Save, and Export. The drum sample list and the sample arrows, CLEAR on the drums, switching pages, presets, and everything you play. Switching drum kits stays open too: the DRUM KIT arrows, and Load in Drum styles, which loads the kit and closes the window. Another tap on the chip goes back to PRO.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p02-sound-live-w630.jp: Poster: Two Keyboards, Live. The Sound screen with two keyboards (16 keys) and LIVE mode, which locks some buttons on stage.

tipsBeginner: MIDI saves the notes you play, so you can edit them later. WAV saves the sound exactly as you hear it, so you can share it.
A knob's gold arc starts at the lower left, and 12 o'clock is the middle of its range. On L/R knobs the arc starts at 12 o'clock, the center.
On a phone the app stays upright, in portrait. On a tablet it can rotate.
groups.tipAdvanced: Some actions have no button of their own, only a long-press: a rhythm number (repeats), a Sound FX slot (tone), a Loop page number (name and color), Presets (quick save), Drum Kits (Random genre), and a saved session (rename).

groups.title: Sound
body: Sine, Square, Triangle, Saw, and Noise sit under the scopes. A tap turns a wave on or off. Tap others to add or remove them, so several waves sound together. One wave always stays on. Both keyboards play the lit waves. The screen starts on Saw.
A tap on Detune turns detune on or off. A tap on RIP, FUZZ, PHAZ, or PIANO turns that one on or off.
Volume, Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release, Cutoff, Resonance, Echo Mix, and Glide are the knobs on the sound screen. A tap on the number opens a box where you type a value.
Drive is the slider on the sound screen. A drag sets the drive amount.
A tap on -1 lowers the octave by one, down to -2. A tap on +1 raises the octave by one, up to 2. A wave with its own octave stays where you set it.
The keys read D, R, M, F, S, L, S, L. The number under a key is its Hz. They start at 222, 299, 333, 355, 396, 444, 463, and 477 Hz.
A tap on + opens a second keyboard above the first, one octave higher. The same + is on the Pad screen, and the second keyboard stays open when you switch between Sound and Pad.
The arrows beside PRESET load the next or previous saved preset. If none are saved, the phone says No saved presets.
The arrows beside DRUM KIT load the next or previous kit. They work in LIVE too.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p01-sound-w630.jpg: Poster: Play Your Own Sound. The Sound screen with five waveforms, envelope, filter and echo.

sections.title: Octave per wave
body: A long-press on a wave key opens an octave panel for that wave alone, under the wave row. Its keys run from -2 to +2. DEFAULT makes the wave follow the main octave again.

The panel does not cover the keyboards, so you can keep playing and hear each pick right away. SAVE keeps the octave. CLOSE puts back what the wave had when the panel opened. A long-press on another wave moves the panel to it and keeps the first wave's octave.

A wave with its own octave shows it in a small badge on its key, such as -2. That octave is fixed: -1 and +1 on the Sound screen move only the waves on Default. With two keyboards, the upper one still plays one octave higher.
Leaving the Sound screen keeps the octave and closes the panel. Presets, sessions, and the preset page file keep the octave of each wave. An older preset or session loads with every wave on Default.

imageAlts.assets/guide/wave-octave-phone.jpg: The Sound screen with the SQUARE · OCTAVE panel open under the wave row: keys -2, -1, 0, +1 and +2 with -2 lit, then DEFAULT, SAVE and CLOSE. The square wave key shows -2, the saw wave -1 and the noise key +2. Two keyboards below.
imageAlts.assets/guide/octave-badges-phone.jpg: The Sound screen with one keyboard and all the knobs. The wave row shows octave badges: -2 on the square wave, -1 on the saw wave and +2 on the noise key. The main octave reads Oct: -2.
imageAlts.assets/guide/octave-badges-dual-phone.jp: The Sound screen with two keyboards, the upper one an octave above the lower one, and the same octave badges on the wave keys: -2, -1 and +2.

sections.title: Sound FX
body: A tap on FX opens Sound FX. The keys still play while it is open.

There are 8 effects: Sub Forge, Depth Drop, Bass Clamp, Floor Pump, Iron Growl, Psy Orbit, Thick Vein, and Kick Bond. A tap turns one on. A tap on the one that is on turns FX off. Only one is on at a time.
You can switch effects while you play. The change is smooth and the volume stays about the same. You hear the effect in the speakers, in a WAV recording, and in what the looper records.
The effects follow the drum beat. Before the drums have played, they run at 120 BPM. After the drums stop, they keep the last drum tempo. Depth Drop drops again every 2 beats and on each new note.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that effect. Each of the 8 effects keeps its own settings when you switch. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 and changes all 8 effects, Sub Forge included.

sections.title: Presets
body: A tap on Presets opens Presets, with 8 slots. Pages 1 to 8 are at the top. Under them are the page name and Edit page name, which changes it.

A long-press on Presets saves the current sound into the preset that is loaded, and the phone says Preset saved. If no preset is loaded, it says No preset loaded. When the window opens, it shows the page of the loaded preset.
A tap on Load opens the saved sound in that slot. A tap on Save stores the current sound there. A tap on Edit changes the name.

Save also stores the settings of all 8 Sound FX and which effect is on. Load brings them back exactly. Factory 64 presets and older presets load without changing the Sound FX. Save also stores which waves are on, and Load lights them again. An older preset lights only its one wave.
Under the page name, Import picks a page file and Save asks the phone where to store the page as a file. The page file also keeps which waves are on and the octave of each wave.

imageAlts.assets/guide/presets-phone.jpg: The Presets, 8 slots window: page keys 1 to 8 with 4 marked, the page name with an Edit page name key, Import and Save keys, eight rows numbered 1 to 8 each with Load, Save, and Edit, one row marked, and a Close key.

sections.title: Key and scales
body: A tap on Key opens Scales. Pick Scale off, or a root from C to B under Major or Minor. A pick closes the window, and Key stays lit while a scale is on.

imageAlts.assets/guide/scales-phone.jpg: The Scales window: a Scale off key, then Major and Minor, each with the roots C, C#, D, E flat, E, F, F#, G, A flat, A, B flat, B. C Minor is marked. A Close key is at the bottom.

sections.title: Custom Frequency
body: Custom Frequency is the first row in Settings. A tap opens Tune frequencies (Hz).
Each key shows its frequency in Hz. Set the keyboard to the frequencies you want, or play from a template.
Ready scales (D = 261 Hz) are the templates: Major, Minor, Harmonic, Dorian, Mixolydian, Hijaz, Kurd, and Pentatonic. A tap on a name applies that template, with D at 261 Hz.

Under the templates, My Presets has 8 buttons with your own names. A tap on one loads its frequencies into the keyboard and selects it. Save stores the current frequencies in the selected preset, or in the first empty one when none is selected. Save* means there are changes that are not saved yet.
Reset is on the title row. Default is above Close.

imageAlts.assets/guide/custom-frequency-phone.jpg: The Tune frequencies (Hz) window: eight frequency fields D, R, M, F, S, L, S, L, a Reset key, Ready scales (D = 261 Hz) from Major to Pentatonic, My Presets 1 to 8, Save, Default, and Close.

tipsBeginner: RIP brightens the sharp top edge. FUZZ adds dirty distortion. PHAZ adds a whooshy swirl. PIANO moves the tone toward a piano. Turn one on, play, and listen.

Attack is how fast a note starts. Release is how long it fades after you let go. Cutoff sets how bright the sound is, and Resonance adds a sharp color near the cutoff, so turn it only a little. Glide slides from note to note.

A scale only marks the keys that belong to it. It does not change the frequencies. Oct moves the whole keyboard up or down and keeps the relations between the keys. A wave with its own octave stays where you set it.
groups.tipAdvanced: Sound FX comes after WARM and after the P, G, and A keys, and before Drive. So Drive pushes the effect too. The speakers, the looper, and a WAV recording all hear the same result.

groups.title: Pad
body: KEY, MIC, LOOP, and DRUM are the targets: they choose which sounds the pad moves. A tap turns a target on or off, and several can be on. KEY starts on.
The pad is marked L, R, HIGH, and BASS. Touch and drag to move the sound.
WAH, OCT, and Vibrato are knobs under the pad, from 0% to 100%. A drag sets them. They shape only the keyboard sound, not the drums, the loops, or the Mic.
A tap on SUB turns it on or off. The hint reads Bass -1 oct.
A tap on WARM turns it on or off. The hint reads Analog warm.
A tap on VIBE turns it on or off. The hint reads Soft vibrato.
P, G, and A sit in the voice row, on both Sound and Pad. P pumps the sound like a trance duck. G chops it like a techno gate. A adds a slow frequency shift. You can turn on more than one.
Hold 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, or 1/32 to stutter the targets that are on, at the drum BPM. Release, and the stutter stops. Hold STOP to fade the targets out for as long as you hold it.

A tap on +, next to the voice row, opens a second keyboard above the first, one octave higher. The same + is on the Sound screen, and the second keyboard stays open when you switch between Pad and Sound. Another tap closes it.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p03-pad-w630.jpg: Poster: A Live Performance Pad. The Pad screen: drag on the pad to shape the sound in real time.

tipsBeginner: Hold a note first, then drag on the pad. The sound follows your finger while the note plays.
When you lift your finger, the pad glides back to the center, so the sound returns to normal by itself.
With the second keyboard open, the WAH, OCT, and Vibrato knobs hide to give the keys room. Close it to get them back.
groups.tipAdvanced: Turn on LOOP and DRUM as well as KEY. Holding a division then stutters the drums and your loops together, in time with the drum BPM, and holding STOP drops them out too.

groups.title: Drum
body: A tap on PLAY starts the drums from the beginning. Another tap stops and returns to the start.
A tap on +4 shows FX 1, FX 2, FX 3, and Voice and hides the keyboard. The key then reads -4. Another tap hides those rows and brings the keyboard back.
A drag on Drum Vol sets the drum volume from 0% to 100%. A tap on the number lets you type a value.

A drag on Swing sets swing from 0% to 100%. A drag on BPM sets the tempo from 60 to 200. BPM, Swing, and the row volumes are live: a change you make while the drums play stays when the next pattern starts.
Hold 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, or 1/32 to repeat the drums at that division while you hold it. Release, and that repeat stops. Hold STOP to silence the drums for as long as you hold it.

A tap on a rhythm number, 1 through 8, loads that rhythm, including its tempo, swing, the sample on each row, the six sound knobs, the volumes, and left and right. Switching to another rhythm saves the one you leave into the current kit. If the rhythm you switch to is empty, it starts as a full copy of the one you came from, and REDO can undo the copy. A long-press on a rhythm number opens Pattern repeats.

A tap on CLEAR, next to RANDOM, clears the steps of the current rhythm, sets its repeat count back to Default, and saves it. Its samples, volumes, and left and right stay. REDO can bring back the steps and the count. A tap on RANDOM builds a new pattern in the chosen genre.
Each row has 16 steps. A tap turns a step on or off.
REDO, in the drum header, steps back through your drum changes: steps, samples, volumes, left and right, the sound knobs, and the rhythm. Each tap goes back one step.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p07-drums-w630.jpg: Poster: Build the Beat. The Drum screen with up to 8 channels and 16 steps, and a built-in sample for each channel and rhythm.
imageAlts.assets/guide/drum-tab-phone.jpg: The Drum screen with the Vinyl Dust kit: STOP, REDO, DRUM FX and DRUM KITS at the top, the DRUM KIT and SAMPLES arrows, the Drum Vol, Swing and BPM knobs, 1/4 to 1/32 and STOP, rhythms 1 to 8 with CLEAR and RANDOM, and the Kick, Snare, Hi-Hat and Perc rows with LOAD, arrows, a volume slider and 16 steps each. A keyboard below.

sections.title: Rows and samples
body: The rows are Kick, Snare, Hi-Hat, Perc, FX 1, FX 2, FX 3, and Voice. A tap on a row name opens a sound list for that row, from all the Factory kits, from the Exclusive kits when they are in the app, and for Voice also from Authentic. The LOADED tab holds your own samples for that row. Each row lists only its own kind of sound: FX 1 to FX 3 share one list, and Voice lists vocals only. A tap on a sound puts it on the row and the list stays open. While the drums play you hear it on the next hit. When they are stopped it plays once. The ◀ and ▶ arrows next to Load step to the previous or next sound. A tap on Load picks an audio file from the phone, adds it to the row's LOADED bank, and puts it on the current rhythm.
A drag on the row slider sets that row's volume. A drag on L/R moves the row between L and R.
SAMPLES sits next to DRUM KIT and shows the sample of the last row you used. Its arrows step that row to the previous or next sample.
The sound list of each row has a waveform of the current sample and six knobs under it: GAIN, SQUEEZE, ATTACK, SUSTAIN, RELEASE, and REVERB.

GAIN adds 0 to +18 dB. SQUEEZE runs from 0 to 100 and flattens the dynamics. ATTACK fades each hit in over 0 to 200 ms. SUSTAIN sets how much of the sample is held, from 0% to 100%. RELEASE fades it out over 5 to 2000 ms and is heard only when SUSTAIN is under 100%. REVERB sends 0% to 100% into the drum reverb.
Each row of each rhythm keeps its own sample and knobs, and they are saved with the rhythm into the kit.

imageAlts.assets/guide/drum-loaded-trim-phone.jpg: The Voice sound list on the LOADED tab: NOW: MY VOICE · LOADED, a LOAD key showing 1 / 88, the sample MY VOICE at 4.73 s, PAGE 1 / 1 · 1 SAMPLES, a waveform trimmed to 1.10 s to 4.13 s with a start and end bar, six knobs, and SAVE, RESET, RENAME, DELETE and CLOSE.

sections.title: Your own samples (LOADED)
body: LOADED is the last tab in each row's sound list, after FACTORY and EXCLUSIVE, and after AUTHENTIC on Voice. Each of the 8 rows has its own bank of up to 88 samples, saved by itself. The samples sit 10 to a page, with arrows to turn pages.

LOAD at the top of the LOADED tab picks one file or several at once, and shows how many samples the bank holds, out of 88. A file that is already in the bank is not added twice, it is selected. A file longer than 30 seconds keeps its first 30 seconds. The last file added goes on the current rhythm.

The bar under the waveform sets where the sample starts and ends, and the part that is kept is shown in seconds. The original file never changes. Trim works on the samples in the list, also Factory, Exclusive, and Authentic.

SAVE keeps the trim and the six knobs with the sample, and every rhythm of the loaded kit that uses it on that row gets them. RESET puts back the full length and neutral knobs: SAVE keeps that, Close undoes it. Close without SAVE goes back to what the sample had. Picking a sample brings its saved trim and knobs to the row.

RENAME and DELETE work on LOADED samples only. A name has up to 24 characters. DELETE asks first, and every rhythm that used the sample goes back to the kit's own sample. LIVE locks LOAD, RENAME, and DELETE.
Sessions and the kit file you export from Drum styles carry the LOADED samples your rhythms use, with their names, trims, and knobs, so they open on another phone.

imageAlts.assets/guide/drum-loaded-rename-phone.jp: The RENAME SAMPLE window over the Voice LOADED tab: the name MY VOICE, the hint Up to 24 characters, and CANCEL and SAVE.

sections.title: Kits and styles
body: The arrows beside DRUM KIT load the next or previous kit. They work in LIVE too.

A tap on Drum Kits opens Drum styles. A long-press opens Random genre, and that is what HOLD says. A tap on Rock, Trance, Rap, or Techno saves that genre and closes the window. Random on this screen uses that genre, and it starts as Rock. That window does not build a pattern by itself.
A tap on Switch to exclusive moves between the factory pages and the Exclusive pages.
There are 8 factory pages and 11 Exclusive pages. Each page has 8 kits. A tap on a page number only shows that page. The kit loads when you tap Load.
A tap on Load loads that kit. A tap on Save stores the current kit under that name. A tap on Edit changes the kit name.
A tap on Edit page name changes the page name. A tap on Import picks a style file. A tap on Export asks the phone where to store the page.

You can load a kit while the drums play. Sounds that still ring fade out in about 20 ms, so there are no clicks or distortion, and volume and pan glide to the new values in about 10 ms. New hits use the new kit at once. A WAV recording hears the same clean change.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p08-drum-styles-w630.j: Poster: Drum Styles. The Drum Styles window with 8 style packs and 11 Exclusive pages, with 1,000+ built-in samples.

sections.title: Drum FX
body: A tap on Drum FX opens Drum FX.
A tap on a preset selects it. A tap on the selected preset turns it off.
The presets are Street Boom, Vinyl Dust, Soft Chamber, Psy Drive, Techno Crush, Tribal Bloom, Goa Gate, and Wire Glitch.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that preset. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 semitones. Those sliders stay only while that preset stays selected.

imageAlts.assets/guide/drum-fx-phone.jpg: The Drum FX window: the line Long-press a preset for Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb, eight round preset icons from Street Boom to Wire Glitch with Street Boom selected, and below them sliders for Amount (72%), EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose (0 semitones), and Reverb (0%).

sections.title: Pattern repeats
body: A long-press on a pattern number opens Pattern repeats. The line under the title reads: How many times the pattern repeats before the next.

A tap on 1 through 10 sets that count. For a higher count, type 1 to 88 in the field beside the infinity mark and confirm on the phone keyboard. A number above 88 becomes 88. A tap on the infinity mark keeps it repeating. A tap on Default clears the repeat. Any pick closes the window.

RHYTHM, with COPY and PASTE, shows only when you open this window from the Drum screen. COPY copies the rhythm whose number you long-pressed. PASTE puts the copy into that rhythm and replaces its steps, samples, volumes, left and right, and sound knobs. That rhythm keeps its own repeat count, BPM, and swing. REDO can undo a paste. PASTE is off until you copy. COPY and PASTE close the window.

imageAlts.assets/guide/drum-repeats-phone.jpg: The PATTERN REPEATS 1 window from the Drum screen: keys 1 to 10, the 1-88 field showing 88, infinity, DEFAULT, RHYTHM with COPY and a dimmed PASTE, and CLOSE.

tipsBeginner: You can change steps while the pattern plays. You do not need to stop. Start the drums, then fix what feels off.
Your drum work saves itself: when you switch rhythm or kit, leave the Drum screen, send the app to the background, or save a session.
Random builds a pattern from the rules of the chosen genre. It is not pure noise. Pick a genre with a long-press on Drum Kits, tap RANDOM, and edit only what feels off.
groups.tipAdvanced: Chain rhythms into a song. Give rhythms 1, 2, and 3 a repeat count, such as 4. The drums play rhythm 1 four times, then 2, then 3, then back to 1. Rhythms left on Default are skipped when the drums move on, and infinity stays on a rhythm until you change it.

groups.title: Loop
body: There are 32 looper channels: 8 pages, 1 to 8, with 4 channels on each page. A recording can run up to 30 minutes. At 30:00 it stops by itself.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p06-looper-w630.jpg: Poster: Build Layers of Loops. The looper with 32 channels across 8 pages, named and colored.

sections.title: Pages and channels
body: A tap on a page number, 1 through 8, shows that page. A long-press opens Page name. Type a name, pick one of 8 colors (orange, red, gold, brown, green, blue, purple, pink), and tap OK. Reset removes the color. Cancel keeps the old name and color.
The page color fills that page number and colors the channel waves on that page.
The name field next to Redo shows the name of the page you are on. A tap in it lets you type the name. Names and colors are saved with the loop project and in Export.
Each channel name starts as Ch and a number. A tap in the name changes it.

imageAlts.assets/guide/page-name-phone.jpg: The Page name window: a Name field, Page color with 8 colors (orange, red, gold, brown, green, blue, purple, pink) and red marked, a Reset key, and Cancel and OK keys.

sections.title: Recording and playing
body: A tap on Rec starts recording. Another tap stops the take. If the channel already had a take, Redo can bring it back.

A tap on Play plays the channel. Play stays off when the channel is empty, unless it is already playing or recording. While the drums play, Play waits for the start of the next drum bar. Starting, stopping, and volume changes are smoothed.
A tap on Stop stops that channel for good. While the drums play, the rhythm boxes in Loop Editor do not start it again. It plays again only when you tap Play on that channel.

M mutes the channel and S solos it. M sits above the FX circle, and S sits above L/R. S turns gold while it is soloed, and every channel that is not soloed goes quiet, on all 8 pages. You can solo several channels. A second tap on S takes the channel out of solo, and when none is soloed everything plays again. A channel that is both muted and soloed stays silent. M is saved with the session. S is not saved, so a load starts with no solo.
The channel waveform keeps moving while the channel is muted or not soloed, so you still see the take. It shows the take before Vol, M, and S.
A tap on Redo brings back the take you lost most recently on this screen: one you cleared, recorded over, or trimmed in Loop Editor. It does not work while that channel is busy.
A drag on Vol sets the volume from 0% to 100%. A tap on the number lets you type a value.
A drag on L/R moves the sound between L and R.

sections.title: Files and projects
body: A tap on Load picks an audio file for the channel. A tap on Save asks the phone where to store the channel as a wav file. Save stays off when the channel is empty. A tap on Clear clears the channel and its Loop Editor settings, and Redo brings back both.
A tap on Import picks a project file and loads the whole loop project. A tap on Export asks the phone where to store the whole loop project.

sections.title: Loop Editor
body: A tap on a channel's waveform opens Loop Editor. It works when the channel has a take and is not recording. A channel with saved edits gets a gold frame. You hear the changes while you edit.
Trim sets the part of the take to keep. Loop sets where the loop starts and ends.

Drum rhythms: 8 boxes, one for each drum rhythm. They choose which rhythm plays with the loop and how many times it repeats. A short press turns a box on, so the loop plays with that drum rhythm, or off again. A long press opens Pattern repeats for that box: 1 to 10, a field where you type 1 to 88, infinity, or Default, which turns the box off. When the drums play, the channel follows the boxes that are on. With no boxes on, the channel keeps looping on its own.

KEEP PLAYING, at the bottom of that window, makes the box play the whole take. Each time the drums enter that rhythm, the take plays once from start to end, even if the drums move on or stop. A count of 3 gives the first 3 entries one play each, and the count starts over when the drums play from the start or you switch kits. With infinity, the take plays again and again while the drums stay on that rhythm, then plays to its end. Turning KEEP PLAYING on for a box that is off lights the box with a count of 1. Without it, a drum STOP fades the channel out gently instead of cutting it.
LOW, MID, and HIGH run from -30 dB to +30 dB. MID HZ moves the middle band from 100 Hz to 8 kHz. GAIN and SQUEEZE run from 0 to 100.
Reset sets everything back to the start values. Close leaves without saving. Save keeps the changes, and a trim cuts the take. Redo can bring back the take from before the trim.
The editor settings are saved with the loop session and in the exported project.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p05-loop-editor-w630.j: Poster: Edit Every Loop. The Loop Editor: trim, repeat, EQ, and lock it to the drum rhythm.
imageAlts.assets/guide/keep-playing-phone.jpg: The PATTERN REPEATS 1 window opened from a Loop Editor rhythm box: keys 1 to 10, a field marked 1-88, infinity lit, DEFAULT, KEEP PLAYING with its gold light on, and CLOSE.

sections.title: Looper FX
body: Looper FX opens from FX on a loop channel.
A tap on a preset selects it. A tap on the selected preset turns it off.
The presets are Hook Glue, Spoken Soft, Indie Wash, Trance Stack, Phrase Throw, Double Lane, Pulse Gate, and Dust Weave.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that preset. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 semitones. Those sliders stay only while that preset stays selected.

imageAlts.assets/guide/looper-fx-phone.jpg: The Looper FX window: the same hint line, eight round preset icons from Hook Glue to Dust Weave with Indie Wash selected, and below them sliders for Amount (91%), EQ Low (66%), EQ Mid (71%), EQ High (57%), Mid-sweep (62%), Transpose (0 semitones), and Reverb (36%).

tipsBeginner: A loop records your keyboard sound as it is at that moment, with your Sound FX. Changing waves, Drive, or Detune later does not change a take you already recorded.
While a channel records, your moves on the Pad are recorded with it. They replay with the loop. To change them live, turn on LOOP on the Pad and touch it.
In the editor, GAIN 50 is the original level. 0 is silent, and 100 adds 12 dB.
groups.tipAdvanced: With at least one rhythm box on, the channel plays only while the drums are on one of those rhythms, and stays silent on the others. A box set to 3 plays the loop 3 times when the drums enter that rhythm. Infinity keeps it going as long as the drums stay there. With KEEP PLAYING on, the take always plays to its end, even when the drums move on.

groups.title: Mic
body: A tap on Redo brings back the take you lost most recently on this screen: one you cleared or recorded over. It does not work while that channel is busy. Mic and Loop keep separate restores.
A tap on Monitor turns the monitor on or off. If it is on and headphones are not connected, the phone warns about speaker feedback.
Gain, Mon, HPF, Gate, Low, Pres, and Comp sit under the heading. Gain runs from 1x to 4x. HPF runs from 40 Hz to 240 Hz. A tap on the number lets you type a value.
Channel names start as Vocal 1, Vocal 2, Vocal 3, Guitar, Bass, and Inst 3. A tap in the name changes it.
A tap on Rec starts recording. Another tap stops. A tap on Play plays the channel. Another tap stops. If the channel already had a take, Redo can bring it back.
A tap on Stop stops that channel for good, the same way as in the Looper. It plays again only when you tap Play on that channel.

S sits left of the FX circle, and M sits right of it, next to Vol. They work like M and S in the Looper. Solo covers the Mic channels only: the Mic and the Looper each have their own solo. M is saved with the session. S is not.
The channel waveform keeps moving while the channel is muted or not soloed. It stops only when the channel itself stops.

A tap on Clear clears the channel and its Mic Editor settings, and Redo brings back both. A tap on Save asks the phone where to store the channel as a wav file. Save stays off when the channel is empty.
HPF and Pres on the channel affect only that channel. The channel has no Gate knob.
A drag on Vol sets that channel's volume. A drag on L/R moves the sound between L, the center, and R.
A tap on Import picks a project file and loads the whole mic project. A tap on Export asks the phone where to store the whole mic project.

imageAlts.assets/posters/en/p04-mic-w630.jpg: Poster: Record Your Voice. The Mic screen with three vocal channels, guitar, bass and instrument, each with its own sound editor.

sections.title: Mic Editor
body: A tap on a channel's visualizer opens Mic Editor. It works when the channel has a take and is not recording.
It is the same editor as Loop Editor: Trim, Loop, the 8 drum-rhythm boxes, EQ, Gain and Squeeze. A long press on a box opens the same Pattern repeats, with the 1 to 88 field and KEEP PLAYING.
Save keeps the changes with the mic project. Redo can bring back a take from before a trim.

imageAlts.assets/guide/keep-playing-phone.jpg: The PATTERN REPEATS 1 window of the editor rhythm boxes, shown here from the Looper, the same as in Mic Editor: keys 1 to 10, a field marked 1-88, infinity lit, DEFAULT, KEEP PLAYING with its gold light on, and CLOSE.

sections.title: Mic FX
body: A tap on Mic FX opens Mic FX for that channel. Under the name it shows FX, and Off or the preset number.
A tap on a preset selects it. A tap on the selected preset turns it off.
The presets are Street Punch, Phone Line, Talk Clarity, Neon Throw, Pulse Delay, Twin Voice, Garage Slap, and Wire Grit.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that preset. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 semitones. Those sliders stay only while that preset stays selected.

imageAlts.assets/guide/mic-fx-phone.jpg: The Mic FX window: the same hint line, eight round preset icons from Street Punch to Wire Grit with Street Punch selected, and below them sliders for Amount (72%), EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep (all 50%), Transpose (0 semitones), and Reverb (0%).

sections.title: Lyrics
body: A tap on Lyrics opens Lyrics. The window opens paused.
A tap on Edit lets you change the words. Done leaves editing. A tap on Play starts the scroll.
A tap on A- makes the text smaller. A tap on A+ makes it larger. A drag on Speed sets the scroll from 20 to 150. It starts at 60.
The X and Close close the window and keep the words.

imageAlts.assets/guide/lyrics-phone.jpg: The Lyrics window: Play, A- and A+ keys, Done and a close X at the top, a Speed slider set to 20, an empty text box that says Paste lyrics here, and a Close key at the bottom.

tipsBeginner: Mic has six channels on two pages. The keys 1 and 2 at the top switch pages.
The first time you tap Rec, the phone asks for the microphone. Allow it. Do a short test take before a long one. With Monitor on, use headphones, or the speaker feeds back into the mic.
HPF cuts low rumble. Gate turns the mic down when you are quiet. Pres raises or lowers the bright, high part of the voice.
groups.tipAdvanced: Transpose in Mic FX shifts the pitch of your voice without changing its length, from -12 to 12 semitones. At 0 the voice is left untouched.

groups.title: Settings and sessions
body: A tap on Language closes Settings and opens Choose language. Continue applies the language.
A tap on Show tutorial starts the tour again.
A tap on Factory 64 asks Restore Factory 64? Restore replaces the Factory 64 presets, all 8 Style drum packs, and all 11 Exclusive packs, then loads slot 1 on page 1. Cancel closes the question.
A tap on Benchmark, under Factory 64, opens the audio test tool.

imageAlts.assets/guide/settings-phone.jpg: The Settings window, titled Language and console session, with New session, Custom Frequency, Language, Save as, Load, Show tutorial, Factory 64, Benchmark, and a Close key.

sections.title: Sessions
body: New session is the first row. It asks for a session name, then empties the Looper and Mic channels. Kits, rhythms, and presets stay. If the name is already taken, it asks before it overwrites.

A tap on Save as opens Save Console. A saved session also keeps the Sound FX and the loop page names and colors. It also keeps the frequency presets, the drum sample picks, the Factory and Exclusive drum banks, the LOADED samples your rhythms use with their trims and knobs, the saved settings of the other samples, the octave of each wave, which waves are on, the two-keyboard view, the pad targets, and the lyrics. With Export all and Import all, the whole setup moves to another device.

Saving, loading, exporting, and importing a session each open a window with a progress bar and the real percent. It stays at 99% until the work is truly finished, and it cannot be closed while the job runs. A second job is refused with the message Another session action is still running.
A tap on Load opens Load Console.
Each saved session is a row with its number and its full name on one line. Under the name are four keys: LOAD, SAVE, EDIT, and X.
LOAD loads that session. Before a session loads, the app asks first and keeps an automatic backup of the current presets and drum kits. Mic monitor is off after a load.
SAVE replaces that session with the current setup, after you confirm with Overwrite. Cancel closes the question.
EDIT renames the session, and a long-press on the row does the same. If the new name is already taken, it asks before it overwrites.
X deletes the session, after it asks Delete session?

Export all saves every session as one file. Export selected saves only the highlighted session as one file. Import all and Import session both read a file you exported. An imported session with the same name as one on the phone gets a new name instead of replacing it.
A tap on a row highlights it. The Load key at the bottom loads the highlighted session, and Cancel closes the window.

imageAlts.assets/guide/load-console-phone.jpg: The Load Console window: two saved sessions, each with Load, Save, Edit, and a red X key, the first one highlighted. Below are Export all, Import all, Export selected, Import session, and the Cancel and Load keys.

tipsBeginner: A Preset keeps one sound. A session keeps the whole project: the loops, the Mic channels, the drums, and the presets.
The tour has a menu of stations. You can skip, resume where you left off, or finish from the menu.
Export all makes one file with every session. Keep it as a backup, or use it to move to another phone with Import all.
groups.tipAdvanced: Restore Factory 64 overwrites any changes you made in the Factory presets and in the Style and Exclusive drum packs. Save a session first: it keeps your presets and drum banks, so you can load your version back.

factory64.title: L Studio
factory64.subtitle: Eight Pages. Sixty-Four Voices.
intro: A complete sound library for L Studio: eight loadable pages, eight named presets on each page. Every voice is written to the app's native page format - volume, ADSR, cutoff, resonance, echo, glide, waveform, octave - on the instrument's home scale (222, 299, 333, 355, 396, 444, 463, 477 Hz).
Built for trance, techno, rap, trap, and metal. No generic "init" slots. Each page is a single musical job.
factory64.includes: 8 JSON pages · 64 named presets · ready to import from Preset
factory64.coverAlt: L Studio Factory Pack eight preset pages grid: Black Well, Gold Hammer, Light Knife, Gray Engine, Low Snake, Saw Teeth, Gold Fog, Spikes
factory64.oneLineList: BLACK WELL - subs · GOLD HAMMER - hits · LIGHT KNIFE - trance leads · GRAY ENGINE - techno · LOW SNAKE - 808 / trap · SAW TEETH - metal · GOLD FOG - pads · SPIKES - plucks
factory64.storeBlurb: L Studio Factory Pack - 8 pages, 64 voices. Black Well for sub and weight. Gold Hammer for hits. Light Knife for trance leads. Gray Engine for techno loops. Low Snake for 808 and slide. Saw Teeth for metal riffs. Gold Fog for pads. Spikes for plucks and stabs. Import one page at a time from Preset. Named, tuned, and voiced for the instrument - not converted from another synth. Plus: 8 Pro drum kits, including Experimental with 8 loaded channels.

pages.name: BLACK WELL
pages.body: Sine and triangle subs at octave -2 (key one sits at 55.5 Hz), plus saw basses with the filter shut. Long release, little echo, glide only where the note should crawl.

pages.name: GOLD HAMMER
pages.body: Synthetic percussion. Noise and square, attack at 5-6 ms, sustain near zero. Cutoff is the material: door at 700 Hz, hammer at 1400, wood at 1900, tin at 3400, whip at 4800, glass at 7800.

pages.name: LIGHT KNIFE
pages.body: Open saw and square leads. High cutoff, high sustain, echo as hall not wash. Octave +1 on the top voice. Rise and pull use slower attack and glide.

pages.name: GRAY ENGINE
pages.body: Stable oscillators for patterns. Cutoff stays in the 900-2800 Hz working band so the filter still moves. Resonance is the character, not decoration.

pages.name: LOW SNAKE
pages.tagline: Trap and rap. 808, slide, dark pluck.
pages.body: Sine 808s at 55.5 Hz. The tail is release, not decay. Slide is 160 ms glide. Concrete is the dry cut. Whisper is the quiet mix bass.

pages.name: SAW TEETH
pages.tagline: Metal and dark techno. Raw blade.
pages.body: Saw, square, and noise. Mid-low cutoff, resonance 0.36-0.58. Drive-oriented voicing. Low riffs at -1/-2, sparks at the top.

pages.name: GOLD FOG
pages.body: Slow attack (180-420 ms), long release (900-1800 ms), echo 0.20-0.38. Sine and triangle. Volume kept down because sine hits harder in this engine.

pages.name: SPIKES
pages.body: Attack 5-6 ms, sustain 0.06-0.16. Short notes that speak on the grid: trance bolt, techno step, trap ember, bell tail.

factory64.listenNote: Low frequencies are barely audible on phone speakers. For the full experience, use headphones or suitable speakers.
factory64.synthsIntro: Eight synth preset pages. Each page is one musical job, eight named voices.
factory64.launchNote: Coming soon to Google Play. L Studio Pro, $8.

factoryDrums.title: 8 drum kits.
factoryDrums.intro: 8 different kits, each with 8 drum styles. That is 64 styles in all, not 64 separate kits. From a rough acoustic sound to electronic rhythms and Experimental. Each kit brings a different character to L Studio Pro.
factoryDrums.closingBody: From acoustic Boom-Bap, through Indie, Techno, and Goa, to Experimental with 8 channels and built-in rhythms.
factoryDrums.closingLine: L Studio Pro lets you choose the sound that fits your direction and start creating.

kits.name: RAP 90'
kits.body: Acoustic Boom-Bap drums from the 1990s, with a warm, rough sound and an organic feel.

kits.name: HIP-HOP 2000s
kits.body: A mix of organic drums and 808, with an urban character and the energy of early-2000s hip-hop.

kits.name: SOFT INDIE
kits.body: Soft, intimate drums, brushes and delicate textures, with a kick that stays present.

kits.name: PSY PROGRESSIVE ROCK
kits.body: A mix of organic rhythms, percussion, and psychedelic energy, from the earth to space.

kits.name: BERLIN 90s TECHNO
kits.body: Dry, hard drums with an industrial character and a hypnotic groove inspired by 1990s techno.

kits.name: TRIBAL AMBIENT TRANCE
kits.body: Organic rhythms that build gradually, from mist and a first pulse, through a ritual and a peak, then a calm.

kits.name: GOA TRANCE
kits.body: Powerful electronic rhythms with a gradual build, from the first pulse to the energy peak.

kits.name: EXPERIMENTAL
kits.body: The most complex kit in the collection. 8 channels, including Kick, Snare, High, Perc, Bass, Texture, FX, and Vocal, with built-in rhythms and automatic transitions.

exclusive.title: Eleven packs.
exclusive.intro: A separate line from the eight Factory Drums kits. Eleven drum packs, each with 8 channels and 8 styles. Whoever buys Pro also gets the Exclusive pack free, at no extra cost, and there is no download button.
exclusive.homeTitle: Eleven special packs. Included with Pro.

items.title: Coming soon to the store: version 1.11 with your own drum samples, Keep playing, and an octave for each wave
items.ticker: Coming soon to the store: version 1.11, up to 88 of your own samples on every drum row, with trim
items.summary: Coming soon to the store, version 1.11: a LOADED bank of up to 88 of your own samples on every drum row, with trim and saved knobs for every sample. Also Keep playing in the Loop and Mic editors, pattern repeats up to 88, an octave for each wave, and switching drum kits in LIVE. Sessions carry the loaded samples to another phone.
imageAlts: The Voice sound list on the LOADED tab: NOW: MY VOICE · LOADED, a LOAD key showing 1 / 88, the sample MY VOICE at 4.73 s, PAGE 1 / 1 · 1 SAMPLES, a waveform trimmed to 1.10 s to 4.13 s with a start and end bar, six knobs, and SAVE, RESET, RENAME, DELETE and CLOSE.
The PATTERN REPEATS 1 window opened from a Loop Editor rhythm box: keys 1 to 10, a field marked 1-88, infinity lit, DEFAULT, KEEP PLAYING with its gold light on, and CLOSE.

sections.title: Drums
bullets: LOADED: a new tab in the sound list of all 8 rows, with a bank of up to 88 of your own samples on each row.
LOAD on the LOADED tab picks several files at once. A file that is already in the bank is selected, not added twice. A file longer than 30 seconds keeps its first 30 seconds.
Trim with a start and end bar under the waveform, on the samples in the list. The original file never changes.
Every sample remembers its trim and its six knobs. SAVE, RESET, RENAME and DELETE in the sound list.
Pattern repeats: a field for any count from 1 to 88, next to 1 to 10, infinity and Default.
CLEAR also sets the rhythm's repeat count back to Default, and REDO brings both back.

sections.title: Loop and Mic editors
bullets: KEEP PLAYING in Pattern repeats: when the drums enter that rhythm, the whole take plays to its end, even if the drums move on or stop.
The same 1 to 88 field for every rhythm box.
Without Keep playing, a drum STOP fades the channel out gently.
Clear on a channel also clears its editor settings, and Redo brings both back.

sections.title: Sound
bullets: A long-press on a wave key opens an octave for that wave alone, from -2 to +2, with DEFAULT, SAVE and CLOSE. The keyboards keep playing while it is open.
A badge on the wave key shows its octave. Presets, sessions and the preset page file keep it.
The preset page file now also keeps which waves are on.

sections.title: LIVE
bullets: The DRUM KIT arrows and Load in Drum styles work in LIVE, so you can switch kits while you play.
Loading, renaming and deleting drum samples stay locked in LIVE.

sections.title: Session
bullets: A session carries the LOADED samples its rhythms use, with their names, trims and knobs, and the saved settings of the other samples, so it opens on another phone.
A drum kit file you export carries its LOADED samples too.

sections.title: Fixes
bullets: Typing a value on a knob: the box no longer closes when the phone keyboard opens.
MIDI recording with several waves on saves one note for each key press.
No click at the end of a Keep playing take.

items.title: Coming soon to the store: version 1.10 with Loop Editor, recordings up to 30 minutes and full session saving
items.ticker: Coming soon to the store: a new Loop Editor, also for Mic, with trim, EQ, and a choice of which drum rhythm plays with the loop and how many times it repeats
items.summary: Coming soon to the store, version 1.10: a new loop editor and the same Mic Editor, recordings up to 30 minutes, full session saving with New session, presets in the Custom Frequency window, a drum sample picker with Factory, Exclusive and Authentic for Voice, and per-rhythm drum samples with auto-save. Also six sound knobs on every drum row, Copy and Paste of rhythms, Clear and Redo on the drums, and new hardware-style keys and windows. Also Mute and Solo on Looper and Mic channels, Load Console with LOAD, SAVE, EDIT and delete for each session, and real progress when saving and loading. Also much lower memory use.
imageAlts: Poster: Edit Every Loop. The Loop Editor: trim, repeat, EQ, and lock it to the drum rhythm.

sections.title: Looper
bullets: Recording up to 30 minutes. It stops by itself at 30:00.
While the drums play, Play starts at the next drum bar.
No clicks when a channel starts or stops, or when you change the volume.
Drive changes smoothly when you move it while you play.
Back is now Redo, in the looper and in Mic. It brings back a take you recorded over or cleared. In the looper it also brings back a take from before a trim.
STOP on a channel stops it for good. The rhythm boxes do not start it again. Play starts it.
M (mute) and S (solo) on every channel. Solo works across all 8 pages, and a second tap on S restores. M is saved with the session.
The channel waveform keeps moving when the channel is muted or not soloed. It stops only when the channel stops.

sections.title: Mic
bullets: M and S on every channel. STOP works the same way as in the Looper.
The top row is cleaner and evenly spaced: no MIC title, and the three monitor slots are gone. Numbers under the knobs are no longer cut off.
The Gate knob on each channel is removed. Gate stays in the monitor row.

sections.title: Loop editor
bullets: Opens when you tap the waveform. Mic Editor opens the same way on a Mic channel.
Trim the recording. Set a loop.

8 drum-rhythm boxes choose which rhythm plays with the loop and how many times it repeats: a short press turns a box on or off, a long press picks repeats (1 to 10, infinity, or Default). With no boxes on, the channel keeps looping.
EQ: Low, Mid, High and Mid Hz. Gain and Squeeze.

sections.title: Drums
bullets: The Swap button is now called Load.
CLEAR, next to RANDOM, clears the steps of the current rhythm. It replaces the drum Save button. Everything is saved automatically.
Each rhythm keeps its own samples, sound knobs, volumes and left and right. Switching rhythms writes them into the current kit.
An empty rhythm starts as a copy of the rhythm you came from.
Six sound knobs per row in each rhythm: GAIN, SQUEEZE, ATTACK, SUSTAIN, RELEASE and REVERB, with a waveform that follows them.
COPY and PASTE a rhythm from the long-press window.
One REDO key steps back through drum changes.
SAMPLES with arrows, next to DRUM KIT, steps the last row's sample.
Switching a drum kit while the drums play is smooth, with no clicks or distortion. A WAV recording hears it clean too.
The Style key is now Drum Kits, with a small gold HOLD above it. A long-press opens Random genre.

sections.title: Pad
bullets: A tap on + opens a second keyboard, shared with the Sound screen.

sections.title: Frequencies
bullets: The Custom Frequency window, opened from Settings, shows the frequencies in full.
8 personal presets.
Save overwrites the selected preset. If none is selected, it saves to the first empty preset.
Tapping a preset loads it immediately.

sections.title: Session
bullets: Saving a session saves the whole workspace, so loading it on another device restores it: frequency presets, drum sample choices, both drum banks, active waves, the dual keyboard, the pad targets and the lyrics.
Before every load there is a confirmation question and an automatic backup. After a load, the mic monitor is off.
New button New session, first in Settings. It asks for a name and clears only the looper and mic channels. Kits, beats and presets stay.
A duplicate name on import gets a new name instead of overwriting the existing one.
Load Console: every session has LOAD, SAVE, EDIT and X (delete, with a question first). The full name is on one line.
Export selected and Import session move a single session.
Saving, loading, exporting and importing show real progress in percent, then success or the reason it failed.
Much lower memory use: takes are stored at their real length, and a session loads as a stream.
Steadier: a Mic recording stops with a message if the microphone is taken away, and the app tells you if some recordings could not be restored.

sections.title: Look
bullets: New hardware-style keys on Drum, Sound and Pad.
New SCALES, PATTERN REPEATS and DRUM STYLES windows. Each drum styles page has its own banner.
A tap turns a wave on or off. One wave always stays on.
The Loop and Mic editor waveforms follow the knobs live.
A gold MM:SS clock shows next to MIDI and WAV while they record.
The drum kits welcome window opens with a new sound: a key click and a light creak.
Hebrew, Arabic and Russian texts updated.

sound-presets.title: Presets: 8 slots, 8 pages
sound-presets.text: A preset keeps the sound with its Sound FX and the waves that are on. A long-press on Presets saves into the preset that is loaded.

sound-scales.title: Key and scales
sound-scales.text: Pick Major or Minor from any root, C to B. A scale only marks its keys. It never changes their frequencies.

mic-channels.title: Channels with their own sound
mic-channels.text: Six channels on two pages. Each one has its own HPF, Pres, FX, volume and L/R, plus mute and solo.

mic-fx.title: Mic FX for each channel
mic-fx.text: Eight presets. A tap selects one, a second tap turns it off, and a long-press opens its sliders, with Transpose from -12 to 12.

loop-looper.title: 32 channels, 8 pages
loop-looper.text: Four channels on each page. A take can run up to 30 minutes, and Redo brings back a take you cleared.

loop-editor.title: Loop Editor
loop-editor.text: Trim the take, set the loop points, and shape it with EQ, Gain and Squeeze. Eight boxes tie the loop to a drum rhythm.

loop-fx.title: Looper FX
loop-fx.text: Eight presets for a channel. A tap selects one, and a long-press opens Amount, EQ, Mid-sweep, Transpose and Reverb for it.

loop-page-name.title: Name and color a page
loop-page-name.text: A long-press on a page number opens Page name. Type a name and pick one of 8 colors. The color also tints that page's waves.

drum-fx.title: Drum FX
drum-fx.text: Eight presets for the drums. A tap turns one on, a second tap turns it off, and a long-press opens its sliders.

drum-repeats.title: Pattern repeats
drum-repeats.text: Pick 1 to 10 repeats or infinity before the next rhythm. COPY and PASTE move a whole rhythm to another number, and REDO undoes a paste.

sound-fx.title: Sound FX
sound-fx.text: Eight effects that follow the drum beat, one on at a time. A long-press opens its sliders: Amount, EQ, Mid-sweep, Transpose and Reverb.

sound-keyboards.title: Two keyboards
sound-keyboards.text: Tap + to open a second keyboard, one octave higher. It stays open when you switch between Sound and Pad.

mic-editor.title: Mic Editor
mic-editor.text: A tap on a channel's visualizer opens it once the channel has a take. Trim, loop, EQ, Gain and Squeeze, with 8 rhythm boxes. Save keeps the changes with the mic project.

mic-lyrics.title: Lyrics teleprompter
mic-lyrics.text: Tap Edit to type or paste your words. Play scrolls them and Pause stops. Speed runs from 20 to 150 and text size from 14 to 48. Everything is saved on the phone.

pad-live.title: Live Pad
pad-live.text: Hold a note and drag on the pad. The sound follows your finger while the note plays. WAH, OCT and Vibrato are knobs from 0 to 100 percent that shape only the keyboard sound.

pad-keyboard.title: Second keyboard on the Pad
pad-keyboard.text: Tap + next to the VOICES row to open a second keyboard, one octave higher. The WAH, OCT and Vibrato knobs hide while it is open.

pad-targets.title: Pad targets
pad-targets.text: KEY, MIC, LOOP and DRUM choose what the pad moves, and several can be on. Hold 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 or 1/32 to stutter them at the drum BPM, and hold STOP to fade them out.

drum-banks.title: Sample banks
drum-banks.text: Eight rows, and a tap on a row name opens its sound list from the Factory and Exclusive banks. Each row lists only its own kind of sound.

drum-shape.title: Shape each sample
drum-shape.text: Six knobs under the waveform shape the sample of that row: Gain, Squeeze, Attack, Sustain, Release and Reverb. Each row of each rhythm keeps its own.

story.title: Всё началось с ноты, которой не было.
body: Есть до, ре, ми, фа, соль, ля и си.
Однажды я спросил себя, почему их только семь.
Вдруг в голове появился ещё один звук. «Аль».
Оттуда родилась первая идея L-Studio. Я хотел сделать клавиатуру, в которой сам смогу задавать, какая частота принадлежит каждой клавише.
Я вообще не планировал делать большое приложение. Я хотел музыкальный инструмент.
Потом я захотел записывать то, что играю, и сделал WAV-рекордер. Потом захотел лупер. Потом барабаны. Потом микрофон.
И каждый раз я спрашивал себя: а почему бы не добавить и это?
Так, шаг за шагом, инструмент превратился в целое приложение для создания музыки.
story.closing: То, что началось с поиска восьмой ноты, стало L-Studio.

featuresIntro.title: Просто открыть и играть.
featuresIntro.body: Не нужно знать музыку, чтобы начать. Открываешь, трогаешь, меняешь, слушаешь и смотришь, что получится.

underHood.title: За кулисами происходит многое.
underHood.body: L-Studio создана, чтобы дать контроль над звуком, не заставляя изучать огромную систему. Клавиши, звук, эффекты, микрофон, лупер, пэд и барабаны работают внутри одного приложения. Можно также вручную настроить частоту каждой клавиши и построить клавиатуру по-своему.
underHood.closing: Сложность живёт в движке. Не в том, как им пользоваться.

justStart.title: Здесь есть чем заняться. Не нужно знать всё сразу.
body: Когда впервые открываешь музыкальную программу, первое, что чувствуешь, это слишком много всего.
Кнопки, окна, меню и всякое, назначение чего непонятно.
L-Studio сделана иначе. Здесь много возможностей, но начать можно без прохождения курса.
Открываешь кнопку. Трогаешь её. Слушаешь.
Через несколько минут уже начинаешь понимать, что каждая вещь делает.

factoryPack.shortText: 8 страниц пресетов. 8 барабанных наборов. Готово к игре.
factoryPack.description: В L Studio Pro есть полный Factory Pack: 8 страниц пресетов синтезатора (64 голоса), затем 8 барабанных наборов, по 8 стилей в каждом (всего 64 стиля, не 64 наборов). Выберите звук или кит, загрузите и играйте.
factoryPack.coverAlt: Обложки паков L Studio Pro рядом: Factory 64 с 64 пресетами на 8 страницах, Drum Kits с 8 наборами и 8 стилями, и Exclusive с 11 ударными паками

vision.title: Я сделал приложение, которое было нужно мне самому.
vision.author: Давид Хатам, разработчик L-Studio
body: Я не из музыкального образования. Я не учился строить профессиональный музыкальный софт, и у меня не было большой системы для работы.
Я просто люблю музыку и хотел управлять звуком так, как это было естественно для меня.
Всё началось с идеи самому задавать частоты клавиш. Оттуда я добавил запись, лупер, барабаны, микрофон и другие вещи, которые были нужны по пути.
Я хочу собрать вокруг L Studio сообщество людей, которые любят музыку. Даже если у тебя нет компьютера или дорогих программ, можно творить на телефоне, который уже есть у тебя в руке.
vision.mainLine: Это для аналоговых людей в цифровом мире.

items.question: L Studio уже в Google Play? И сколько стоит?
answer: L Studio Pro для Android скоро выйдет в Google Play, за $8. Это единоразовый платёж. Версия 1.11 скоро в магазине.
Когда приложение выйдет, купить его можно будет через Google Play. Этот сайт не продаёт приложение, и кнопки скачивания здесь нет.

items.question: Что входит в Pro? Есть бесплатная версия?
answer: Версия приложения одна: Pro. Это всё приложение: Factory Pack с 64 пресетами и восемью наборами ударных, а также одиннадцать паков ударных Exclusive, без доплаты. Кнопки скачивания для Exclusive нет.
В Pro нет рекламы, и всё в нём открыто с первого запуска.
Бесплатное демо скоро выйдет, и его можно будет скачать с этого сайта.
Паки Exclusive можно посмотреть на странице Exclusive этого сайта.

items.question: На каких устройствах работает и на каких языках?
answer: L Studio это приложение для Android. Нужен Android 7.0 или новее, размер 77.4 МБ. Версии для iPhone пока нет.
Приложение проверялось на разных телефонах с Android. На планшетах оно не проверялось, поэтому поддержка планшетов не обещается.
На телефоне приложение остаётся вертикальным, в портретной ориентации.
Приложение на четырёх языках: английском, иврите, русском и арабском. Язык меняется в Settings, в строке Language.

items.question: Работает без интернета? Кто-нибудь видит мою музыку?
answer: Да, оно работает без подключения к интернету. Приложение вообще не запрашивает доступ в интернет.
Единственное разрешение, которое оно просит, это микрофон, при первом нажатии на Rec. Его можно отозвать в любой момент в настройках телефона.
Ваши записи, пресеты и сессии остаются на телефоне или там, куда вы сами их сохранили. В приложении нет рекламы и нет сбора данных об использовании.

items.question: Я новичок. С чего начать?
answer: Откройте приложение и трогайте всё подряд. Курс не нужен.
В Settings пункт Show tutorial запускает короткий тур. У тура есть меню станций: можно пропустить, продолжить с того места, где остановились, или закончить из меню.
В руководстве на этом сайте семь тем. В конце каждой темы три совета новичкам и один совет для продвинутых.

items.question: Как записать и поделиться тем, что я сделал?
answer: В верхней строке две клавиши. WAV записывает то, что вы слышите, так что можно поделиться звуком в точности как он звучит. MIDI сохраняет ноты, которые вы сыграли на клавиатурах, чтобы потом их можно было править.
Нажмите один раз, чтобы начать, и ещё раз, чтобы остановить. После остановки телефон спросит, куда сохранить файл. Во время записи золотые часы показывают минуты и секунды.
В MIDI не входят ударные, лупы и микрофон. Там только то, что вы играли на клавишах.
Чтобы сохранить один канал Looper или Mic как файл WAV, используйте Save на этом канале. Export сохраняет весь проект.

items.question: Можно использовать свои звуки и аудиофайлы?
answer: Да, в рядах ударных и в каналах Looper. У каналов Mic кнопки Load нет: они записывают с микрофона, а Save сохраняет файл WAV.

Ударные: на экране Drum нажатие на название ряда (Kick, Snare и другие) открывает список звуков. Load в ряду выбирает один аудиофайл, а LOAD во вкладке LOADED выбирает один или сразу несколько. У каждого из 8 рядов свой банк LOADED до 88 сэмплов, и текущий ритм играет последний добавленный файл. Любой сэмпл из списка можно обрезать и настроить ручками GAIN, SQUEEZE, ATTACK, SUSTAIN, RELEASE и REVERB, и сэмпл хранит эти настройки.
Looper: Load на канале выбирает аудиофайл для этого канала и заменяет запись на нём. Redo прежнюю запись не вернёт. Каналов 32, по одному файлу на канал.

Какие файлы: любой аудиофайл, который Android на вашем телефоне умеет воспроизводить и декодировать. Собственного списка форматов у L Studio нет, поэтому формат, который телефон не декодирует, не загрузится, и появится сообщение (Could not load audio или Could not load the audio file).
Как читается файл: стереофайл сводится в моно. Любая частота дискретизации преобразуется в частоту приложения, то есть частоту аудиовыхода телефона (44.1 kHz, если телефон её не сообщает).
Длина: для ряда ударных у файла длиннее 30 секунд остаются первые 30 секунд, и приложение об этом сообщает. Для канала Looper файл длиннее 30:00 обрезается на 30:00 без сообщения.
В режиме LIVE Load заблокирован. Чтобы загрузить, вернитесь в PRO.

items.question: В чём разница между Preset и сессией?
answer: Preset сохраняет один звук, включая то, какие волны включены, октаву каждой волны и настройки Sound FX. Долгое нажатие на Presets быстро сохраняет текущий звук в загруженный пресет.

Сессия сохраняет весь проект: лупы, каналы Mic, ударные, пресеты, Sound FX, имена и цвета страниц Loop, пресеты частот, выбор сэмплов в ударных, сэмплы LOADED, которые используют ритмы, цели Pad и текст песни.
New session очищает каналы Looper и Mic. Наборы, ритмы и пресеты остаются.

items.question: Как сделать резервную копию или перейти на новый телефон?
answer: Откройте Load Console из Settings. Export all сохраняет все сессии одним файлом, а Export selected только выделенную сессию. Храните файл ещё и вне приложения.
На новом телефоне используйте Import all или Import session и выберите файл. Импортированная сессия с уже существующим именем получает новое имя и не заменяет старую.
У проекта Looper или Mic отдельно есть Export и Import на его экране. У пресетов и стилей ударных есть свои Save, Export и Import в их окнах.

items.question: Что такое Load Console?
answer: В Settings нажатие на Load открывает Load Console. Каждая сохранённая сессия это строка с номером и именем, а под именем четыре клавиши: LOAD, SAVE, EDIT и X.

LOAD загружает сессию. Перед загрузкой приложение спрашивает и делает автоматическую копию ваших текущих пресетов и наборов ударных. SAVE заменяет сессию текущей настройкой после подтверждения в Overwrite. EDIT переименовывает, и долгое нажатие на строку делает то же самое. X удаляет после вопроса.
Сохранение, загрузка, экспорт и импорт показывают полосу прогресса с настоящим процентом и понятное сообщение об успехе или ошибке. Пока идёт работа, окно закрыть нельзя.

items.question: Есть скрытые действия, которые стоит знать?
answer: Да. У некоторых действий нет своей кнопки, только долгое нажатие или удержание.
Presets (экран Sound): долгое нажатие быстро сохраняет текущий звук в загруженный пресет.
Клавиша волны на экране Sound: долгое нажатие открывает октаву этой волны.
Номер ритма на экране Drum (от 1 до 8): долгое нажатие открывает Pattern repeats, с COPY и PASTE.
Drum Kits (экран Drum): удержание открывает Random genre, где выбирается жанр для RANDOM.
Номер страницы в Looper: долгое нажатие открывает имя и цвет страницы, из 8 цветов.
Пресет в Sound FX, Drum FX, Looper FX или Mic FX: долгое нажатие открывает Amount, EQ, Transpose и Reverb для этого пресета.
Строка сессии в Load Console: долгое нажатие переименовывает.
Ячейка ритма в Loop Editor или Mic Editor: долгое нажатие выбирает, сколько раз этот ритм повторяется, до 88, и KEEP PLAYING.
1/4, 1/8, 1/16 и 1/32 на Pad и на экране Drum: удерживайте, чтобы повторять в темпе BPM ударных, отпустите, чтобы остановить. Удержание STOP приглушает звук.
Число под ручкой: нажатие открывает окно, где можно ввести точное значение.

items.question: Как превратить несколько ритмов ударных в целую песню?
answer: Долгое нажатие на номер ритма открывает Pattern repeats: выберите от 1 до 10 повторов, введите до 88 или выберите бесконечность или Default. Задайте ритмам 1, 2 и 3 значение 4, и ударные сыграют ритм 1 четыре раза, потом 2, потом 3 и вернутся к 1.
Ритмы с Default пропускаются. Бесконечность остаётся на ритме, пока вы его не смените.

Чтобы скопировать ритм: долгое нажатие на ритм, который нужно скопировать, и COPY. Потом долгое нажатие на ритм, который нужно изменить, и PASTE. Вставка заменяет шаги, сэмплы, громкости и ручки звука, а у ритма остаются свои число повторов, BPM и свинг. REDO отменяет вставку.

Каналы Looper тоже могут идти за ритмами: включите ячейки ритма в Loop Editor, и канал играет только пока ударные на одном из этих ритмов. С включённым KEEP PLAYING запись всегда доигрывает до конца, даже когда ударные идут дальше.

items.question: Что такое PRO и LIVE в верхней строке?
answer: PRO обычный режим, где всё открыто. LIVE блокирует некоторые кнопки, чтобы вы могли сосредоточиться на игре, а случайное нажатие не стёрло запись и не загрузило файл.
LIVE блокирует Clear в каналах Looper и Mic, Load в рядах ударных и в каналах Looper, загрузку, переименование и удаление сэмплов LOADED, имена каналов и страниц, Import и ввод числа на ручке.
Открытыми остаются Rec, Play, Stop, mute и solo, Save, Export, переключение страниц, пресеты, смена наборов ударных и всё, что вы играете. Ещё одно нажатие на значок возвращает PRO.

items.question: Я случайно стёр запись или записал поверх. Можно вернуть?
answer: Да. На экранах Loop и Mic рядом с клавишами страниц есть клавиша Redo. Она возвращает запись, которую вы потеряли последней на этом экране: стёртую, записанную поверх или обрезанную в редакторе. Пока канал занят, она не работает.
У Looper и у Mic своё восстановление.
На экране Drum REDO в заголовке отступает на одно изменение за нажатие: шаги, сэмплы, громкости, левое и правое, ручки звука и ритм, включая CLEAR и вставку.

items.question: Как работает Custom Frequency? Можно настроить свой строй?
answer: Да. В Settings первая строка Custom Frequency открывает Tune frequencies (Hz). У каждой клавиши показана частота в Hz, и её можно задать любой. Клавиши начинают с 222, 299, 333, 355, 396, 444, 463 и 477 Hz.
Если нужна отправная точка, есть шаблоны: Major, Minor, Harmonic, Dorian, Mixolydian, Hijaz, Kurd и Pentatonic, с D на 261 Hz. Нажатие на название применяет шаблон.
В My Presets 8 кнопок с именами на ваш выбор. Save сохраняет в них текущие частоты, а пресеты частот сохраняются и в сессии.
Клавиша Key на экране Sound это другое: она только отмечает, какие клавиши входят в гамму, и не меняет ни одной частоты.

items.question: Можно сохранить микротональную игру в MIDI? Можно подключить MIDI-клавиатуру?
answer: Да, но это запись в файл. Клавиша MIDI сохраняет файл MIDI с нотами, которые вы сыграли на клавиатурах. Каждый звук сохраняется как ближайшая нота плюс Pitch Bend, который возвращает отклонение от точной частоты. Файл рассчитан на диапазон Pitch Bend в два полутона.

Чтобы услышать микротональный строй, программа, открывающая файл, должна поддерживать Pitch Bend и быть настроена на два полутона. Ноты, которые звучат вместе, получают каждая свой канал MIDI, чтобы у каждой сохранился свой изгиб.
Пока L Studio не поддерживает внешнюю MIDI-клавиатуру, и в ней нет живого MIDI, ни входа, ни выхода. Это запланировано на потом, без даты.

items.question: Запись с микрофона тихая или звук возвращается. Что делать?
answer: Если тихо: увеличьте Gain, он идёт от 1x до 4x и начинается с 2x. Потом проверьте Vol канала, от 0% до 100%. Когда запись есть, нажмите на визуализатор канала и откройте Mic Editor: в GAIN значение 50 это исходный уровень, а 100 добавляет 12 dB.
Если звук возвращается: при включённом Monitor пользуйтесь наушниками. Без наушников телефон предупреждает об обратной связи через динамик.
HPF срезает низкий гул, от 40 Hz до 240 Hz. При первом нажатии на Rec телефон просит доступ к микрофону. Если вы отказали, разрешите его в настройках телефона.

items.question: Сколько есть каналов и какие ограничения?
answer: Looper: 32 канала, то есть 8 страниц по 4 канала. Запись может идти до 30 минут, а на 30:00 она останавливается сама.
Mic: шесть каналов на двух страницах. Запись может идти до 4:00 на трёх каналах первой страницы и до 3:00 на трёх каналах второй страницы. На пределе она останавливается сама.

Ударные: 8 рядов (Kick, Snare, Hi-Hat, Perc, FX 1, FX 2, FX 3 и Voice), 8 ритмов в каждом наборе и 16 шагов в каждом ряду. У каждого ряда есть ещё банк LOADED до 88 ваших сэмплов, до 30 секунд каждый, а число повторов ритма доходит до 88.

items.question: Есть задержка звука или треск. Что можно сделать?
answer: L Studio просит у Android аудио с малой задержкой на Android 8.0 и новее. На Android 7.0 и 7.1 приложение работает без этого запроса, поэтому задержка может быть больше.
Задержка зависит и от самого телефона. В Settings, под Factory 64, Benchmark открывает инструмент проверки звука.
Если треск или задержка не проходят, напишите в поддержку: модель телефона, версия Android и версия приложения.

items.question: Как получить помощь и что с возвратом денег?
answer: Пишите на dudichatam@gmail.com. Полезно указать модель телефона, версию Android, версию приложения и что вы делали.
Этот сайт ничего не продаёт, и у него нет собственных правил возврата. Когда приложение выйдет, покупка будет через Google Play, а с вопросами о покупке можно писать на тот же адрес.
Что изменилось в каждой версии, видно на странице Updates этого сайта.

finalCta.title: Может, пора найти свой звук.
finalCta.body: Можно начать с одного звука, ритма, лупа или маленькой идеи. Ты никогда не узнаешь, что получится, пока не начнёшь играть.
